question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the actual synthesis and production of breast milk?
explanation: Prolactin is secreted by the anterior pituitary gland to stimulate milk production in the alveoli. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h1)

question: What triggers the physical release of milk from the alveoli during breastfeeding?
explanation: Suckling stimulates oxytocin release, which causes the tiny muscle cells around the milk glands to squeeze milk forward. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h1)

question: When does normal breast engorgement usually happen after a mother gives birth?
explanation: This is the time when mature milk comes in and blood flow to the breasts peaks. A totally normal part of the journey! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h2)

question: Why is gentle hand expression of milk recommended before feeding when a mother's breasts are very swollen (engorged)?

options.A: It softens the areola so the infant can achieve a proper latch
options.B: It replaces the need for any future breastfeeding sessions
options.C: It cures underlying bacterial infections instantly
options.D: It permanently stops milk production in the affected breast

explanation: Severe swelling pulls the nipple flat, making it tricky for the baby to grip. Expressing a little milk first creates a softer surface to grasp. Well done! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h2)

question: A nursing mother complains of sharp nipple pain and visible cracks. What should you as a nurse check first?

options.A: Suggest weaning the baby to formula immediately
options.B: Recommend applying strong antiseptic ointments before every feed
options.C: Assess the infant's latch technique and mouth positioning during feeding
options.D: Advise the mother to stop breastfeeding completely for one week

explanation: Fixing how the baby takes the breast stops further damage and lets the skin heal naturally. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h3)

question: Which sign helps you tell the difference between a simple blocked milk duct and acute mastitis?

options.A: Presence of a hard lump in the breast
options.B: Absence of systemic fever and chills
options.C: Slight pink coloration of the skin

explanation: Blocked ducts cause local discomfort, but they don't give the body-wide fever and chills that come with an active infection. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h4)

question: What exactly is a lactocele?

options.A: A milk-filled cyst formed from a blocked duct
options.B: An acute bacterial infection of the milk glands
options.C: A normal physiological swelling during milk let-down
options.D: A malignant tumor common in postpartum women

explanation: A lactocele is simply a pocket containing trapped milk that forms when a duct stays blocked. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a body-wide (systemic) symptom of puerperal mastitis?
explanation: Mastitis causes painful inflammation and blocked flow—definitely not clear and painless! Spotting this makes you a sharp clinician. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h5)

question: Why must a mother with mastitis keep removing milk from the infected breast?

options.A: Pumping removes the need to take prescribed antibiotics
options.B: Stopping milk removal cures the infection faster
options.C: Continued drainage prevents further milk stasis and reduces infection severity
options.D: It prevents the baby from getting any nutrition

explanation: Emptying the breast stops milk from sitting stagnant, which is what bacteria love. Keeping it flowing helps her heal faster! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h5)

question: What physical sign helps a nurse tell a breast abscess apart from simple mastitis?

options.D: General warmth across the entire chest

explanation: An abscess forms a walled-off pocket of pus that feels spongy or bouncy (fluctuating) under the fingers. Spot on! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h6)

question: What is the main medical treatment needed for a diagnosed breast abscess?

options.C: Surgical drainage of pus combined with antibiotics

explanation: Antibiotics alone can't clear a walled-off pocket of pus, so the trapped fluid needs to be safely drained. Excellent clinical reasoning! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h6)

question: When is the best time for nurses to start teaching mothers about proper breastfeeding and preventing complications?

options.B: During antenatal and early postnatal periods
options.C: Only after a breast abscess has formed
options.D: When the child is weaned to solid foods

explanation: Early teaching gives mothers the right techniques before any trouble starts. Prevention is always better than cure! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h7)

question: Why is getting enough rest emphasized as a way to prevent breast infections in nursing mothers?

options.A: Rest stops the baby from crying during the night
options.B: Lying down automatically cures blocked milk ducts
options.C: Sleeping prevents milk from ever being produced in the alveoli
options.D: Fatigue lowers the immune response, making the body more prone to infection

explanation: When a new mother is exhausted, her immune system struggles to fight off invading bacteria. Rest is vital care! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h7)
